title: "Contraband parcel" arrest threat vs. genuine customs duty notice
summary: A caller from SwiftShip Couriers phones about an international parcel addressed to the recipient that is held at customs. In the legitimate case, the parcel is a gift from a relative abroad, customs has assessed duty on it, and the agent explains that the duty is paid through SwiftShip's official duty-payment process (or the parcel can be refused). In the fraud case, the caller says the parcel contains illegal items, that a case is being registered against the recipient, and that the recipient must transfer money to a given account to "verify" themselves and avoid arrest. Both callers say "customs", "parcel held", and ask the recipient to pay. The words do not decide the label.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult who is not sure whether a relative has sent them something; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Parcel: an international parcel addressed to the recipient; sender described vaguely ("from abroad").
Both callers give an agent name and the airway bill number.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller claims the recipient faces arrest over a parcel and demands a money transfer to an account to settle or "verify" the matter. Customs duty is not paid to settle criminal allegations, and no genuine agency asks for a transfer over a phone call to avoid arrest.
stable_facts: The caller says the parcel contains prohibited items and that a case will be registered in the recipient's name.
The caller says the matter is "confidential" and says an officer will "handle" it; any officer persona is described, not scripted.
The account is given as [ACCT_LAST4] at Kaveri Bank or as [UPI_ID_4], described as a "verification" or "security" account, with a promise that the money will be returned.

legitimate.label_rationale: The agent tells the recipient that customs has assessed duty on a gift parcel and explains how to pay it through SwiftShip's official process, with a receipt, or to refuse the parcel. There is no threat, no personal account, and the recipient can decline.
legitimate.caller_objective: Get the duty paid (or a refusal recorded) so the parcel can be delivered or returned.
stable_facts: The parcel was declared as a gift; customs has assessed duty of [AMOUNT_3].
The duty appears against [AWB_ID] on SwiftShip's tracking page with a customs reference; payment is made there, or to the delivery agent against a printed receipt.
The agent says the recipient may refuse the parcel, in which case it is returned to the sender.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may restate urgency, insist on confidentiality, or say the money is refundable. Intimidation must stay at the level described in this card: no detailed impersonation of named agencies, no scripted interrogation, no instructions to stay on video. They must not switch to asking for OTPs, remote-access apps, or card details. The legitimate agent must not mention police, arrest, or any account outside SwiftShip's process.

must_preserve: customs" and payment wording in both cases
arrest/case threat and transfer to an account in _F
duty, receipt, and refusal option in _L
may_vary: parcel's declared contents in _L (clothes, sweets, small electronics)
the recipient's guess about the sender
must_not_emit: real officer names or badge numbers

ambiguities: Genuine international parcels do attract duty that the consignee must pay; a payment request about customs is not evidence of fraud.
The recipient's uncertainty about the sender is the same in both cases and must not be used as a cue.
Real duty rates vary; the amount is kept in the same range for both cases so that amount cannot predict the label.
If generation shows only the threat (F-E1) and ends before the payment demand, the prefix must be rejected.

evidence_references.claim: Fraudsters call about a parcel "containing drugs or contraband" and demand money to settle the "case" (CE03)
Callers threatening arrest are not police/CBI/Customs; report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in (CE04, C12)
Gifts imported through courier are dutiable and consignees pay or refuse (CE05)
Couriers file the entry and duty is paid online through the customs courier system (CE06)
The customs courier portal warns of phishing calls from unauthorised persons (CE07)
